title: GeoJSON Coordinate Counter: Vertex Census
description: Count every coordinate vertex across a GeoJSON object's points, lines and polygons with the GeoJSON Coordinate Counter. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a four-feature sample file (two points, one line, one square) holds exactly 9 coordinate pairs — 1 + 1 + 2 + 5 — the square costing five because its ring closes.
quick_answer: The GeoJSON Coordinate Counter inspects how many coordinate vertices a GeoJSON object contains, across points, lines and polygons alike. Paste the file and read the census: the vertex count that drives file weight, rendering cost and simplification decisions — the dataset’s true size beneath its feature count.

Two Points (1 each), one LineString (2), one closed square ring (5: four corners plus the repeated first point). Total 9. Every GeoJSON census decomposes this way — the counter shows its working by geometry family.
One national outline feature can hold a million vertices while a whole city dataset holds fifty thousand. Feature counts applaud the wrong file; vertex counts tell the rendering truth.

popular_table.note: Closing vertices (the repeated first point of a ring) are counted — they are really in the file, really parsed and really drawn. The counter counts the file as it is, not as it might be idealised.

How does count relate to file size?
Roughly linearly for geometry-heavy files: each vertex costs its digits plus separators. The minified-size tools turn the estimate into bytes.
Can it break the count down by type?
The census totals the object; pairing it with the Geometry Type Counter reconstructs most of the picture (features per type × their vertices).
